newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA sees yields under pressure.
newsitem.headline: SIA sees yields under pressure.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) said on Monday it expected its passenger traffic to remain strong but added that yields would continue to come under pressure from the strength of the Singapore dollar.

SIA said in a statement with its half-year results to September 30, 1996, that growth in air cargo traffic was likely to be sluggish as the main export economies in the Asia-Pacific region were decelerating. It was particularly concerned about the cyclical downturn in the electronics industry.

"With capacity being added to the market at a faster pace than traffic growth, and the strong Singapore dollar, it is unlikely that cargo yields will improve in the short-term," the statement said. "No significant surplus from the sale of aircraft is envisaged for the second half of the current financial year," it added.
In a separate statement, SIA quoted deputy chairman and chief executive Cheong Choong Kong as saying the airline had been buffeted by escalating fuel prices in the six months.
"While there may be some respite on the currency front, the direction of fuel prices in the second half is uncertain, as is the recovery of the cargo market," it quoted Cheong as saying.
